content.text:
# Next.js dashboard. Build context is the REPO ROOT (see docker-compose.yml there)
# because the dashboard depends on the backend workspace package
# `@daz-pilot/daz-pilot-backend-api-types` via a `file:` path. That package must
# be built first so the `file:` install resolves to compiled output.

# ---- Stage 1: Build the shared api-types package ----
FROM node:22-alpine AS apitypes

WORKDIR /repo/backend

COPY backend/package.json backend/package-lock.json ./
COPY backend/workspaces/backend-api-types/package.json ./workspaces/backend-api-types/
COPY backend/workspaces/backend-utils/package.json ./workspaces/backend-utils/
COPY backend/workspaces/database/package.json ./workspaces/database/
COPY backend/workspaces/core-backend/package.json ./workspaces/core-backend/
COPY backend/workspaces/database-migrator/package.json ./workspaces/database-migrator/

RUN npm ci

COPY backend/tsconfig.base.json backend/tsconfig.json ./
COPY backend/workspaces/backend-api-types/ ./workspaces/backend-api-types/

RUN npm run build --workspace=@daz-pilot/daz-pilot-backend-api-types

# ---- Stage 2: Install dashboard deps & build ----
FROM node:22-alpine AS build

WORKDIR /repo/dashboard

# The `file:` dependency resolves to ../backend/workspaces/backend-api-types, so
# the built package must sit at that path before `npm ci`.
COPY --from=apitypes /repo/backend/workspaces/backend-api-types /repo/backend/workspaces/backend-api-types

# .npmrc sets `install-links=true`, which makes npm copy the `file:` dependency
# into node_modules (instead of symlinking). The lockfile was generated with this
# setting, so npm ci needs it to stay in sync — and it makes the build/runtime
# self-contained (no symlink to the backend workspace at runtime).
COPY dashboard/package.json dashboard/package-lock.json dashboard/.npmrc ./
RUN npm ci

COPY dashboard/ ./

# next.config.ts runs validateEnv() at build time, so every URL in envSchema must
# be present. NEXT_PUBLIC_* is inlined into the client bundle, so these must point
# at the host-facing URLs. Override via build args if needed.
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_CORE_BACKEND_DOMAIN=http://localhost:4000
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_CORE_BACKEND_DOMAIN=$NEXT_PUBLIC_CORE_BACKEND_DOMAIN
ENV CORE_BACKEND_DOMAIN=$NEXT_PUBLIC_CORE_BACKEND_DOMAIN

RUN npm run build

# ---- Stage 3: Production runtime (next start) ----
FROM node:22-alpine AS production

WORKDIR /repo/dashboard

ENV NODE_ENV=production
ENV PORT=3000

# install-links=true copied api-types into node_modules, so the built app is
# self-contained — no backend workspace needed at runtime.
COPY --from=build /repo/dashboard /repo/dashboard

# `next start` writes only under .next/cache at runtime (the <Image> optimizer
# caches fetched /media/** responses there, see images.remotePatterns). Only that
# subtree is handed to `node`; app code and node_modules stay root-owned and
# therefore read-only to the runtime user.
RUN mkdir -p .next/cache && chown -R node:node .next/cache

EXPOSE 3000

# `node` (uid 1000) ships with the base image. Port 3000 is unprivileged and no
# runtime write lands outside .next/cache, so the server needs no root.
USER node

CMD ["npm", "run", "start"]
